correctness.rationale: Smooth cubic plane has unique support J(x), whose kernel gives all unit BJ partners y=±(-t²,1)/(1+t^6)^(1/3). Computing J(y)(x) gives the exact D(t). The change u=t³ and symmetry u↦1/u reduce to H(k)=k³(1-k²)/(1+k²)² on [0,1]. Its exact derivative k²(3-6k²-k⁴)/(1+k²)³ has a unique interior sign change at k²=2√3-3, and substitution yields the stated positive radical with all maximizers classified. A normalized duality-map bijection for smooth strictly convex finite-dimensional real spaces exchanges (x,y) with (J(y),J(x)), preserves BJ orthogonality and the reversed residual. This proves the dual value and orbit.
risks: Only finite-dimensional real smooth strictly convex spaces are asserted in the duality lemma.
Finite-sample checks do not establish the maximum; exact differentiation does.

value.rationale: This computes a natural sharp quantitative reversal parameter for a canonical smooth non-Hilbert plane and simultaneously its Hölder dual, including the full ordered maximizing orbit rather than an unsupported scalar guess. The proof isolates a simple unimodal algebraic support-function profile and reveals a general finite-dimensional duality principle for the same C parameter. The result directly sharpens the qualitative approximate-symmetry question introduced by the defining source and distinguishes two inequivalent approximation conventions.
risks: The exact radical is shown only for the two specified exponents; a general ℓp² formula is not claimed.
